thread:
mira: Heads up — NRT pop saw a p99 jump and throughput drop around 10:04 UTC. p99 ~2x baseline, throughput down ~30%. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/obs/nrt?range=10m :thinking:

deploy-bot: deploy: runtime-service v2.14 canary -> completed on nrt-pop at 10:03 UTC by ci/cd (no rollback)

sam: I didn't push any kernel selector code to production. only a tiny batching config tweak in the morning (staging->prod) at 09:50. Not seeing a direct deploy at 10:03 from my side.

anya: looking at host metrics — a-nrt-03 shows sustained proc_steal ~6% starting 10:01. Kernel-selector logs on that host show repeated fallback to compat kernel (reason=kernel_pin_mismatch). Batch size telemetry shows median batch_size per-request dropped to 1 for ~120s -> KV cache hit rate tanked.

ben: uploaded a quick sample flamegraph and perf report: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/perf/2412345678/nrt-flame.svg. Top syscalls are futex/wake, context-switches spike. smells like scheduler contention / noisy VM.

mira: do we have any noisy tenants scheduled on a-nrt-03? any colocated batch jobs?

sam: checking allocations — yes, viz-stream-analytics had a bursty job that started at 09:58 on that host (high user CPU). I throttled it at 10:06 and drained the VM at 10:08. After drain p95 back to normal, p99 trending down.

anya: logs excerpt from kernel-selector around the window:

```
[10:01:54] kernel-selector: host=a-nrt-03 proc_steal=6.1% kernel=fast path_select=fallthrough->compat reason=cpu_steal_threshold
[10:02:03] batching: batch_target=1 observed_latency=312ms kv_cache_miss_rate=0.78
```

anya: KV cache warmup suffered because batch size collapsed and requests hit cold prefixes. This cascaded into higher token latency and more kernel fallback loops.

ben: hypothesis: noisy tenant -> proc_steal -> kernel-selector flips to compat kernel that has higher syscall path (locks/futex) -> batching heuristic sees small effective batch and disables pooling -> higher per-token syscalls -> thrash. Perf traces align.

mira: agreed. temporary mitigation steps that worked: stop/throttle noisy job, drain affected host, tombstone noisy VM. We should add two mitigations: (1) surface proc_steal per-pop in console and alert if >2% sustained, (2) make kernel-selector consider recent batching occupancy and prefer kernels with lower syscall overhead under high steal rather than pure latency benchmarks.

sam: quick mitigation applied at 10:06 (throttle) and 10:08 (drain). deploy-bot: mark incident containment at 10:09.

deploy-bot: incident: containment detected for thread 2412345678 at 10:09 UTC.

anya: suggested code changes / config tweaks:
- batching heuristic: add min_effective_batch = 8 when seq_len < 96 and kernel_selector.state == "compat_fallback"
- kernel selector: add proc_steal_weight (0.5) into scoring, and if proc_steal > 2% bias away from high-syscall kernels
- KV cache: expose per-pop cold_prefix_rate metric to help root cause earlier

ben: I'll open ENG-RUNTIME-3124 with perf reproducer and attach flamegraphs + small QEMU reproducer. Also add a regression test that simulates 5-10% proc_steal and asserts batch_target doesn't collapse to 1.

mira: action items:
1) sam/anya: telemetry + alert for proc_steal per-pop (P0)
2) ben: perf reproducer + ticket (P1)
3) eng-runtime: PR to kernel-selector to include proc_steal in scoring and guardrails on batch collapse (P1)
4) ops: consider autoscaler bump thresholds for pop when KV cache cold_start detected (P2)

sam: noted — I'll draft the telemetry PR and roll a small canary to staging later today. Thanks for the quick triage everyone :thumbsup:

mira: filing a short postmortem after we close the tickets. Keep logs/artifacts in the incident folder: https://incidents.redwood/internal/2412345678. Closing thread once follow-ups are tracked. :white_check_mark:
